title: Under eight percent of records supplied half the residual product sum of squares in four US ozone injury samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We tested whether ozone and soil moisture estimates depend on a small share of forest survey records. We used 5,277 site-years in four Northeast and North Central US samples in 1994-2002 and 2003-2010. A fixed model controlled site, year, weather, visit date, plant count and species count. Only 4.6-7.1 percent of records supplied half the residual ozone by moisture product sum of squares. The highest-leverage five percent supplied 42.7-51.6 percent. Removing those records changed the slope sign in both North Central samples. Removing one year changed signs in the early Northeast and later North Central samples. These are fixed-data design and deletion results. They do not show incorrect records, independent sample sizes or causal plant effects. Original confidence intervals already included zero. The same-source follow-up adds a design audit, not independent biological evidence. Coarse exposure, unmeasured missed injury, fixed site means during deletion and selected indicator plants limit use. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Cumulative partial leverage and slope sensitivity in four forest injury samples. Lines on the right are omit-one-year ranges, not confidence intervals.
